segments.title: How Sanjusangen-do remains contemplative amid mass tourism
segments.summary: Sanjusangen-do shows how a busy Kyoto temple can still give visitors the quiet and space needed for contemplation.
segments.body: ShipShape trips are framed as a way to understand culture as well as history, beyond collecting facts and figures. Sanjusangen-do initially looks like a tourist trap because of the coaches and crowds, yet the temple is quiet enough for reflection even in a busy part of Kyoto. The large tour groups disperse quickly, leaving visitors room to wander through. The visit follows a walk from the National Museum in Kyoto, near the train station, and overturns an expectation that the 600-yen admission would be disappointing. No temple chronology is given; the focus is how a heavily visited religious site can retain a spiritual atmosphere. The visit closes with a running 'zero or 100 percent' theory that Japan either does not care about something or cares for it completely, with temples firmly in the latter category.

evidence.note: He contrasts an initial impression of a tourist trap with the quiet, visitor flow, and contemplative experience preserved inside the temple grounds.
